authority: Operator-directed ticket (plans/fieldwise_tickets.md ticket 1), executing plans/fieldwise_reinstantiation_plan.md steps B3-B7. The operator approved the §2.1 three-way decision-log split on 2026-08-10. Durable recording per CLAUDE.md §9.4 of a state transition that later readers cannot reconstruct from the tree alone. Applies already-ratified rules (§9.1 docs/ is authoritative, §9.2 runtime memory is not constitutional truth, §12.3 contradictions are logged). NOT a constitutional amendment; no §14.5 question is raised here.
why: The FIELDWISE master draft and the superseded Tier 3 describe two different projects. The identity spine matches — fellow, host ELTE Budapest, supervisor, 24-month European Fellowship, Hungary — but the research content does not. Tier 3 had to be replaced, not edited, so every artifact derived from it (Tier 4 run state, all of Tier 5) had to go with it. Leaving derived state behind would let a later phase read the superseded project through a gate that believes it is fresh.

tier4_run_scoped_state.scope_note: The ticket's acceptance list names four directories. preseed/phase8/ and reuse/phase8/ are deleted as well, because they hold the superseded run's excellence, impact and implementation sections. Both paths are opt-in (--preseed-phase8-sections, the reuse policy), so neither blocks a run, but leaving them would let ticket 10's Phase 8 supersede a FIELDWISE draft with the previous project's prose.
tier4_run_scoped_state.graph_compile_deletion: docs/tier4_orchestration_state/graph_compile/ is deleted as a third, separately declared deviation. Its pre_promote_backup/ held a restorable copy of the purged Tier 3, which the promote tool could have written back over a FIELDWISE seed. The directory is gitignored, so this deletion appears in no diff and git cannot restore it. That loses nothing: the purged Tier 3 itself is recoverable from commit 6d96a60, and the staging tree is regenerable by re-running the compiler.
retained: docs/tier4_orchestration_state/reinstantiation_provenance.json — records the milestone-1 purge and the D8 vault absorb. Engine and branch provenance, not demo-run output.
.gitkeep placeholders in phase_outputs/, checkpoints/, validation_reports/, reuse/ so the skeleton stays tracked.

tier5.deleted: All files under proposal_sections/, assembled_drafts/, final_exports/, review_packets/. Only the four .gitkeep placeholders remain.
tier5.consequence: The E4 harness golden-set regression lane pins the deleted Tier 5 content and is now red. Ticket 11 decides between re-freezing the baselines against the FIELDWISE Tier 5 and marking the lane expected-red on this branch.

tier3.deleted: project_brief/, consortium/, call_binding/, architecture_inputs/, integration/ contents; hand_lift_provenance.json; working_assumptions.json.
retained: source_materials/part_b_draft_v0/FIELDWISE_MSCA_Master_Draft.docx — the source of truth for the reseed.

working_assumptions.example.json — an inert, project-neutral template carrying no superseded project data. Proposal_Engine_Operator_Manual.md §168 instructs the operator to copy it to working_assumptions.json, and ticket 6 needs it. Plan step B5 reads 'delete all of Tier 3 except source_materials', which would have removed it; the deviation is deliberate and recorded here.

runtime_memory.authority: CLAUDE.md §9.2 — runtime execution state may be cleared without affecting the constitutional validity of docs/. All of these are gitignored, so the clearing is a working-tree operation and does not appear in this commit.
runtime_memory.what_cleared_means: .claude/runs/ refills with a test-00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000 fixture directory whenever the test suite runs, because tests/test_production_mode.py writes one. Cleared therefore means no demo-run contexts remain, not that the directory stays absent. reinstantiation_provenance.json recorded the same carve-out at the milestone-1 purge ('test-* fixture run dirs preserved').

decision_log_split.rationale: The decision log held 52 files with three different dispositions. A blanket archive would have removed rulings the next run depends on, and a blanket delete would have removed more. Two modules cite entries directly: runner/graph_determinism_check.py cites dod-1c for retaining compiled_at, and runner/checkpoint_publisher.py cites chk-1 for the provenance quad.

deleted.what: Runner-written run state: decision-log-update_*, topic-scope-check_*, gate_failure_*. Each references artifacts this purge deleted, and each is regenerable by the next run.

archived.what: Human decisions about the superseded project. FIELDWISE replaces all five, but each records why an operator chose what they chose, so none is deleted.
archived.load_bearing_move: runner.docx_exporter._synthetic_override_active globs _SYNTHETIC_OVERRIDE_GLOB (decision_log/synthetic-spine*.json) and the exporter stamps a visible 'SYNTHETIC DEMO — NOT FOR SUBMISSION' marker on the exported Part B when the file matches. The glob is non-recursive, so moving synthetic-spine-demo-override_2026-07-13.json into archive/demo-run/ clears the stamp from the FIELDWISE export while preserving the record. Leaving it in place would have marked a real submission as a demo.
archived.dangling_reference: status-vocabulary-correction_2026-07-13.json (retained) carries supersedes_aspect_of pointing at the pre-move path of tier3-hand-lift-msca-pf_2026-07-13.json. The moved-path map above is the resolution; the retained entry is left byte-unchanged because rewriting an engine ruling to chase a path move would edit a record of what was decided.

retained.what: Rulings that govern the engine regardless of which call is written: DOD-1 x4, CHK-1, ST-1, the transport and truncation fixes, the taxonomy-drift correction, the gate-result schema backfill, the agnosticism proof, the E2-E5 and LG-1 harness frameworks, and the rest.

decision_log_split.known_category_tension: The 29 are project-agnostic in rule and project-scoped only in evidence. dod-1e proves checkpoint publication by driving run msca-pf-graph-01, yet the rule binds any run. §5 defines Tier 4 as run-scoped orchestration state, which an engine ruling is not, while §9.4 mandates this location. Moving them to a register outside Tier 4 would need a §14.5 amendment. The operator declined to raise that question on 2026-08-10, so the 29 stay where they are and the tension is recorded, not resolved.
